title: System X: An LLM Decision Model That Replies from Its Own KV Cache
summary: The method replaces a separate full-prompt second LLM call for text replies with continuation from the decision model's existing KV cache after a Jev-style option readout. It costs a LoRA fine-tuning pipeline, routing-data curation, and added serving complexity, and gains remain workload-dependent rather than a fixed multiplicative factor. Failures include state conflicts, unsupported reply details, possible instruction-following degradation from added support data, and reply-judge results confounded by prompt and generation-limit differences.
rationale: For a 24 GB or API-constrained team, the idea is practical to prototype because it reuses a small LoRA-adapted model and can reduce latency, but the mixed quality evidence and remaining failure modes justify a controlled pilot rather than production adoption.
technique: KV-cache reuse for decision-to-reply LLM routing

claims.statement: The method replaces a separate full-prompt second LLM call for text replies with continuation from the decision model's existing KV cache after a Jev-style option readout. It costs a LoRA fine-tuning pipeline, routing-data curation, and added serving complexity, and gains remain workload-dependent rather than a fixed multiplicative factor. Failures include state conflicts, unsupported reply details, possible instruction-following degradation from added support data, and reply-judge results confounded by prompt and generation-limit differences.

Cache reuse saves 15-37% latency on Apple M4 Pro and 17-39% on Qwen3-1.7B; calibration error falls from 0.292 to 0.169; v4 JevBench accuracy rises 55.0% to 61.0% (p=0.04), with no significant IFEval change.
